- [2026-05-12] **Strings use `.get()` (code point) + `.byteAt()` + `.graphemeAt()`**: No `char` type. Default indexing is by Unicode code point. Bytes and graphemes are explicit alternates. See `spec/strings.md`.
- [2026-05-12] **Bracket sugar for `.get()` and `.set()` on all collections AND maps**: `arr[i]`, `m["key"]`, `s[i]` all desugar to `.get()`. Writes via `arr[i] = v` desugar to `.set()`. Strings immutable (no write sugar). Types reject bracket access entirely — forces dot for fields. Reverses earlier no-`map[key]` decision. See `design/collections.md`.
- [2026-05-12] **Iterable contract = two types (`Iterable[T]`, `FallibleIterable[T]`)**: In-memory collections follow `Iterable[T]`; I/O sources follow `FallibleIterable[T]`. Same `for` syntax; compiler infers fallibility from the source's contract and auto-propagates errors when needed. Stdlib adapters `.orSkipFailures()` and `.withErrors()` for ergonomic fallible-to-infallible conversion. See `design/iterables.md` + `spec/iterables.md`.
- [2026-05-12] **Import aliases + duplicate-name compile error**: TS-style `{ name as renamed }` and `namespace as renamed`. Duplicate names (including stdlib-vs-local collisions) refuse to silently pick — compile error forces aliasing. See `design/modules.md` + `spec/modules.md`.

## Active Decisions (Architectural — v0.3-M3 ship entry)

**[2026-06-01] v0.3.0-m3 STAGED, NOT YET RELEASED — user-gated.** All Phases 6-9 complete. Tag = `v0.3.0-m3` (NOT m2 — `v0.3.0-m2` is taken by the M10 Teaching-Surface release, commit `13264af`; release numbers track ship order not roadmap milestone numbers). Cargo.toml bumped `0.3.0-m1` → `0.3.0-m3`. CHANGELOG `[0.3.0-m3]` section written. VSCode `package.json` at `0.3.0-m3`.

**WHY the inference model (the winning design):** `design/future/concurrency.md` documented it all along — whole-program TRANSITIVE may-block analysis from `{sleepAsync}` seed, every transitively-suspending function becomes a stackless state machine, inline poll-and-yield at every suspending call site, composed frames (one `ynz_alloc` per spawned task tree), NO bridge anywhere. The M2 HALT happened because the original plan cut M2/M3 at "state machines | may-block analysis" — an unbuildable line, because the analysis engine is REQUIRED to build the state machine layer. Moving the may-block engine to M2 fixed this. The `block_on` sync bridge (originally "Shape B") was deleted in Phase 8 as a result.

**M2-boundary decisions deferred to M3 (locked):** `WaitInsideLoop` and `LocalCrossesWait` are M3-scope (frame-backed mutable locals transform). Sub-expression suspending calls and non-self mutual recursion are M3-scope (per-frame layout metadata + expression-position suspension). These are compile errors in v0.3-M3, not regressions.

**Next milestone:** v0.3-M3 — cross-module may-block propagation (M8 multi-file query), auto-`wait` insertion (lifts `WaitInsideLoop`/`LocalCrossesWait` via frame-backed locals), expression-position suspension (lifts sub-expression guard), auto-parallelization of independent statements, mutual-recursion mixed-layout frames. See roadmap `v0-3-concurrency-perf.md`.

Only top-level `wait` in `-> nothing` fns spawned from a NON-state-machine caller works (the 8-task concurrency demo). **Root cause of false confidence:** the P0 spike hand-wrote Rust MIMICKING codegen and validated THAT — the real emitted codegen diverges, so the spike ACCEPT (incl. Contracts #4d SM-in-SM, #5 errors-cascade) was on a model, not the product. Phases 0–4 only exercised `-> nothing`/top-level state machines, so the gap hid until P5. **Decision: the thin-slice walk-back (clean-error + defer the rest to M3) is WRONG long-term** — M3 (auto-`wait` insertion) builds ON M2's coroutine substrate, so deferring value-returning + nested suspension to M3 is circular (M3 would have no working foundation). The RIGHT answer = fix the codegen properly (value-returning frames threading the return value through `Poll<T>`; genuine inline poll-and-yield for nested `wait`-SM replacing the panicking block_on fallback; proper background-from-SM spawn-and-drive), driven by a re-spike that validates against the ACTUAL compiler output (compile real `.ynz` through the real compiler — NOT hand-written Rust). This is milestone-hard codegen needing its own plan — NOT a fix-loop on the exhausted Phase-5 session. **Status: Phases 0–4 COMMITTED + sound (`6328666` spike, `b740e3d` runtime, `5109b52` codegen + Option-B clean errors, `5b72521` typeck warnings, `6a2d32d` teaching surface — the working top-level/`if` `-> nothing` `wait` slice is real). Phase 5 NOT committed (its executor worked around the bugs by omitting `errors_cascade_through_state_machine` + 5 SM-from-SM tests and swapping the demo keep-alive from `wait sleepAsync` to blocking `sleepMs` — those workarounds ship broken criteria silently and MUST NOT land). Cargo.toml bump to 0.3.0-m2 is premature + uncommitted. M2 plan stays `active` (BLOCKED). No `/release`.** Next: `/plan` a state-machine-codegen-rework spike+milestone, ideally fresh session. **GRAVEYARD CANDIDATE:** "P0 spike validated a hand-written model that diverged from the shipped codegen → false ACCEPT; later phases only tested the narrow `-> nothing`/top-level path → gap hid until end-to-end integration. Future spikes MUST compile real source through the real compiler, and milestone success criteria MUST have an end-to-end test before any phase claims them met."

- **[2026-05-31] M2/M3 boundary — `wait` nesting scope = OPTION B (clean error, defer transform to M3)** *(narrower than — and folded into — the HALT above; Option B covered wait-in-loop + local-crossing-wait)*: In v0.3-M2, an explicit `wait` works at top level and inside `if`. `wait` inside a `while`/`for`/`match` body, and a `let` local whose value is read after a `wait` (crosses a suspension boundary), emit a CLEAN teaching compile error (WHAT/WHAT-INSTEAD/WHY pointing to M3) — emitted at typeck so the codegen no-op fallback is unreachable. WHY: the full frame-backed-mutable-locals stackless-coroutine transform (flush-before-suspend + reload-at-resume + SM-aware variants of all ~5 `for` forms + `while` + the `let`-crossing dominance fix) is M3-scale machinery; the spike already proved the loop ABI (P0 Contract #7b), so M3 wires codegen onto a proven foundation alongside auto-`wait` insertion. The M2 shipped demo (8 background `pause()` tasks) uses top-level waits only — Option B descopes nothing user-visible. Replaces the prior silent no-op (loop) + codegen crash (let-crossing) — both were bugs — with honest errors. Decided via /execute-plan resume of Phase 2.

- **[2026-06-01 Phase 8] Option-B guards re-confirmed on inference foundation — LOCKED, no escape hatch**: `WaitInsideLoop` and `LocalCrossesWait` STAY M2 compile errors after Phase 7's inference-model rework. Verification: Phase 8 confirmed both guards still fire correctly (exit 1 + clean WHAT/WHAT-INSTEAD/WHY + M3 pointer) on the real compiler. WHY they stay: (1) Frame-backed MUTABLE locals (flush-before-suspend + reload-at-resume) are the genuine M3 hard core — distinct from the Phase 7 typed RETURN slot work; the composed frames back RETURN values + embedded child sub-frames, NOT arbitrary mutable locals crossing a wait boundary. (2) The loop-state transform (save/restore loop counter across suspension) is also M3-scope. (3) Lifting either guard requires Patrick sign-off + a read-AND-mutated-across-wait fixture proving the codegen is correct. No escape hatch: these are NOT safe to remove in M2 even under the inference model. The inference model deciding which functions are state machines does not automatically make arbitrary-mutable-local-crossing-wait safe to emit IR for — the frame layout simply doesn't support it yet. Decision to escalate in M3 planning.

## Active Decisions (Architectural — v0.3-M1)

**v0.3.0-m1 shipped 2026-05-21** — `background` runs on a separate OS thread via Tokio blocking thread pool embedded in `libynz_rt.a`.

**Key architectural decisions locked in this milestone:**
- **C-ABI bridge** (`ynz_rt_init`/`ynz_rt_spawn_blocking`/`ynz_rt_check_preempt`/`ynz_rt_shutdown`): Tokio is internal; users never see Tokio types. WHY: binds the runtime to Yinz's ownership model; future swap (e.g., custom scheduler) is possible without user-facing API change.
- **Stack-alloca ctx (not heap)**: `ynz_rt_spawn_blocking` takes a stack-allocated ctx; runtime copies it synchronously before returning. WHY: no heap ctx means no RAII cleanup concern at the call site; runtime is responsible for the copy lifetime.
- **Loop back-edge preempt (M1) vs call-site preempt (M2)**: M1 inserts `ynz_rt_check_preempt` at loop back-edges only. Call-site insertion measured at 1190% overhead on fib(30) — deferred to M2 with loop-integrated yield strategy. WHY: loop-only gives O(1) preempt cost per iteration; call-site needs smarter insertion logic.
- **`--no-auto-parallel` hidden flag**: plumbed in M1 (no-op); becomes load-bearing in M3 when auto-parallelization ships. WHY: plumb now so M3 isn't a flag-API breaking change.
- **Fire-and-forget only (M1)**: `let h = background fn()` handle form is a compile error. WHY: handles need channels; channels ship in M4. Documented as `background-handle-form` deferred-tooling-feature in registry.
- **Total tests at ship**: ~1220 (across all crates; ynz-typeck 156, ynz-lsp 100+, ynz-driver 120+, ynz-runtime 10, ynz-registry 29, etc.).
